top_3_by_cost_of_inaction.cost: The matrix answers 'missing 0' for every exported account and never surfaces new iCloud data. Silent, optimistic failure on the console's central question: the operator stops rechecking and misses the accounts that gained photos/seeds. Costs the campaign, not just the UI.

Two reconciliation models ship side by side with different numbers (104 vs 124 assets) and an acceptance test that compares the plan's own two derived values. Expensive to unwind later: API, UI and the P0 gate all encode the duplicate, while the working Verify panel keeps contradicting it.

At the plan's own 500-account scale, a queued job can vanish mid-flight; the account sticks at 'exporting' with no row to retry - the exact blind spot P0-1 exists to close. Fix cost is small now and grows once retry/priority are layered on top of a queue that silently loses entries.

drop_if_forced.reason: Lowest independent value: P2, mechanism-visible on the first manual run (three selected accounts finish in reverse), and it rests on an unread client enqueue loop, so it is the one finding a verifier can plausibly refute.
